shelters.name: Animal Refuge League of Greater Portland

shelters.name: Bangor Humane Society

shelters.name: Kennebec Valley Humane Society
shelters.description: Kennebec Valley Humane Society provides compassionate care and adoption services for homeless cats and dogs in central Maine.

shelters.name: Greater Androscoggin Humane Society
shelters.description: Greater Androscoggin Humane Society is the only open-admission shelter in Androscoggin County, providing shelter and adoption services for companion animals.

shelters.name: Midcoast Humane
shelters.description: Midcoast Humane provides shelter, care, and adoption services for homeless animals in Sagadahoc, Lincoln, and surrounding counties in coastal Maine.

shelters.name: SPCA of Hancock County
shelters.description: SPCA of Hancock County is a nonprofit shelter providing care and adoption services for homeless animals in the Bar Harbor and Ellsworth areas.

shelters.name: Franklin County Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Franklin County Animal Shelter is a nonprofit municipal shelter serving Franklin County communities with animal shelter and adoption services.

shelters.name: HART (Homeless Animal Rescue Team) of Maine
shelters.description: HART of Maine is a nonprofit rescue organization dedicated to rescuing homeless cats and dogs and finding them loving forever homes.

shelters.name: Coastal Humane Society
shelters.description: Now part of Midcoast Humane, Coastal Humane Society continues its mission to provide shelter and care for homeless animals in the midcoast region.

shelters.name: P.A.W.S. Animal Adoption Center
shelters.description: P.A.W.S. Animal Adoption Center is a nonprofit, no-kill shelter serving Knox County and surrounding areas with adoption services for cats and dogs.

shelters.name: Responsible Pet Care of Oxford Hills
shelters.description: Responsible Pet Care of Oxford Hills is a nonprofit shelter providing animal welfare services including adoption, spay/neuter programs, and community education.

shelters.name: Ark Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Ark Animal Shelter is a nonprofit shelter serving Washington County, providing care and adoption services for homeless cats and dogs in eastern Maine.

shelters.name: Underhound Railroad
shelters.description: Underhound Railroad is a nonprofit rescue organization transporting homeless dogs from high-kill shelters in the South to loving homes in Maine and New England.

shelters.name: Sato Heart Rescue
shelters.description: Sato Heart Rescue is a nonprofit organization rescuing abandoned satos (street dogs) from Puerto Rico and finding them forever homes in Maine.

shelters.name: Central Aroostook Humane Society
shelters.description: Central Aroostook Humane Society provides shelter and adoption services for homeless animals in northern Maine's Aroostook County region.

shelters.name: Harvest Hills Animal Shelter
shelters.description: Harvest Hills Animal Shelter is a nonprofit organization providing temporary shelter and adoption services for homeless cats and dogs in central Maine.

shelters.name: Passion for Paws
shelters.description: Passion for Paws is a foster-based nonprofit rescue organization dedicated to saving homeless dogs and cats in Maine and finding them loving homes.

shelters.name: Almost Home Cat Rescue
shelters.description: Almost Home Cat Rescue is a volunteer-run, foster-based nonprofit organization dedicated to rescuing and rehoming homeless cats in southern Maine.

shelters.name: Maine Cat Rescue
shelters.description: Maine Cat Rescue is a nonprofit, foster-based rescue organization dedicated to saving homeless, abandoned, and feral cats throughout Maine.

shelters.name: Downeast Humane Society
shelters.description: Downeast Humane Society serves the Ellsworth and Hancock County area with animal welfare services including adoption and community programs.

shelters.name: Waldo County Pet Food Pantry and Humane Society
shelters.description: Waldo County Pet Food Pantry and Humane Society provides food assistance to pet owners in need and helps homeless animals find forever homes.

shelters.name: Lucky Pup Rescue
shelters.description: Lucky Pup Rescue is a nonprofit rescue organization saving dogs from high-kill shelters and transporting them to loving homes in Maine and New England.

shelters.name: New England Lab Rescue
shelters.description: New England Lab Rescue is a nonprofit organization dedicated to rescuing and rehoming Labrador Retrievers and Lab mixes throughout New England including Maine.

shelters.name: Casco Bay Pibble Rescue
shelters.description: Casco Bay Pibble Rescue is a nonprofit organization dedicated to rescuing, rehabilitating, and rehoming pit bulls and bully breeds in Maine.

shelters.name: Maine Greyhound Placement Service
shelters.description: Maine Greyhound Placement Service is a nonprofit organization dedicated to finding loving homes for retired racing greyhounds in Maine and New England.

shelters.name: Town of Sanford Animal Control
shelters.description: Town of Sanford Animal Control provides municipal animal control services including stray animal intake, lost and found pets, and adoption services.

shelters.name: City of Portland Animal Refuge League
shelters.description: Portland Animal Control provides municipal animal services for the City of Portland, working with local rescues to help homeless animals find homes.

shelters.name: Hearts & Tails Animal Alliance
shelters.description: Hearts & Tails Animal Alliance is a nonprofit, foster-based rescue organization dedicated to saving homeless pets in Maine and placing them in loving homes.

shelters.name: Pixie Project Maine
shelters.description: Pixie Project Maine is a nonprofit rescue organization focused on finding homes for special needs and overlooked animals in Maine.

shelters.name: Safe Haven Humane Society
shelters.description: Safe Haven Humane Society is a nonprofit, no-kill shelter providing care and adoption services for homeless cats and dogs in southern Maine.

shelters.name: Animal Welfare Society
shelters.description: Founded in 1967, Animal Welfare Society is the safety net for lost and homeless pets in southern Maine. Provides adoption, veterinary clinic, spay/neuter services, and community education programs.

shelters.name: Humane Society Waterville Area
shelters.description: Located in Central Maine, caring for 2000+ animals every year. Best Friends Animal Society partner providing adoptions for dogs, cats, and small animals.

shelters.name: Charley's Strays
shelters.description: Small, privately run 501(c)(3) no-kill shelter established in 1989. Takes in dogs and cats of all ages, including older and special needs animals other shelters won't accept.

shelters.name: Peace Ridge Sanctuary
shelters.description: GFAS-accredited sanctuary on 1,725 acres home to 600+ rescued farm animals, equines, and companion animals. Winner of 2024 GFAS Outstanding Sanctuary of the Year Award. Founded in 2001.

shelters.name: PALS Cat Shelter
shelters.description: No-kill cat shelter dedicated to helping cats find loving forever homes. Also operates Maine's only low-cost, nonprofit feline veterinary clinic.

shelters.name: The Pixel Fund
shelters.description: Division of Pixel's Posse, a 501(c)(3) all-volunteer rescue saving lives from high-kill shelters through foster network. Operates in Maine, Georgia, and Florida.

shelters.name: Halfway Home Pet Rescue
shelters.description: Feline rescue, sterilization, and rehabilitation center working with Central Aroostook Humane Society to address community cat population challenges. Hosts mobile spay clinics.

shelters.name: The Maine Dog Rescue
shelters.description: Foster and volunteer-based nonprofit saving dogs from high-kill shelters in the South and supporting Maine families rehoming pets. Best Friends Animal Society partner.

shelters.name: NFR Maine - North Florida Rescue
shelters.description: Foster-based dog rescue saving lives from high-kill shelters in Northwest Florida and placing them in loving homes in Maine. All dogs spayed/neutered, vaccinated, microchipped.

shelters.name: Maine Coast Animal Rescue (MCAR)
shelters.description: Female-owned kennel-free nonprofit conducting monthly transport missions to rescue dogs from overcrowded and kill shelters. 7+ years rescuing hundreds of animals.

shelters.name: The Grateful Dog Rescue
shelters.description: Non-profit, all-volunteer foster-based dog rescue saving adult dogs from high-kill shelters. Licensed by State of Maine. Focus on adult dogs who need second chances.

shelters.name: Rescue Charlie's Friends
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) licensed shelter pulling dogs from high-kill shelters in Alabama and Texas. Rescued over 630 dogs in 2024. Has dedicated transport receiving facility.

shelters.name: Grammy Rose Dog Rescue & Sanctuary
shelters.description: 60-acre campus with 6 residential-style dog cabins, wooded trails, and welcome center. Features on-campus ice cream shop and mini golf whose proceeds support operations.

shelters.name: Almost Home Rescue of Maine
shelters.description: All-breed canine rescue 501(c)(3) founded in 2005. Rescues dogs from overcrowded shelters in Mississippi, Louisiana, and North Carolina, as well as local cases.

shelters.name: Coastal Maine Great Dane Rescue
shelters.description: Small home-based rescue group serving Maine and New Hampshire since 2008. Focuses on stray, abandoned, abused, or owner-surrendered Great Danes.

shelters.name: Tall Tails Beagle Rescue
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) beagle/hound rescue founded in 2005. Has rescued hundreds of hounds from overcrowded shelters and Puerto Rico street dogs.

shelters.name: Give a Dog a Home German Shepherd Rescue
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) no-kill rescue founded 2011 saving dogs from high-kill shelters in Texas. Serves as Greater Goods Charities distribution center. Offers Wellness on Wheels program.

shelters.name: Friends of Feral Felines
shelters.description: All-volunteer network addressing feral, abandoned, and stray cats in southern Maine through TNR (Trap-Neuter-Return). Also fosters kittens for adoption.

shelters.name: Rocky Coast Rabbit Rescue & Sanctuary
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) founded in 2024 rescuing and rehoming rabbits across New England. Provides active trapping, responsible rehoming, and educational outreach.

shelters.name: Avian Haven
shelters.description: Wild bird rehabilitation center founded 1999. Treats ~3,000 birds annually from 100+ species. Has treated 34,000+ birds. State and federally permitted, one of largest in New England.

shelters.name: Center for Wildlife
shelters.description: For 39 years has treated 90,000+ injured wild animals. Manages 2,500 patients yearly representing 190+ species. Nature Center open Thu-Sun for public visits.

shelters.name: Saco River Wildlife Center
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) founded 2015 providing rehabilitative care to ill, injured, or orphaned Maine wildlife. Treated 900 animals in 2023. Currently expanding to 18+ acres.

shelters.name: Misfits Rehab
shelters.description: Wildlife rehabilitation center caring for injured, orphaned, or sick wildlife with goal of release back to natural habitat.

shelters.name: Skybird Wildlife Center
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) Wildlife Rehabilitation Center specializing in rehabilitating Maine's wild reptiles and amphibians.

shelters.name: Maine State Society for the Protection of Animals (MSSPA)
shelters.description: Protects health and welfare of neglected and abused equines. Provides 24/7 veterinary access and rehabilitative care for 35-40 equines. Offers adoption and permanent sanctuary.

shelters.name: Rockin' T Equine Sanctuary & Rescue
shelters.description: Registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit equine rescue facility taking in abused, neglected, or surrendered horses and providing compassionate care.

shelters.name: Horses With Hope
shelters.description: Created in 2013 as Maine's largest private horse rescue. Partners with MSSPA offering comprehensive evaluation and retraining program for rescued equines at Broadview Farm.

shelters.name: Ever After Mustang Rescue
shelters.description: Licensed Equine Rescue Facility with 30+ years of mustang experience. Rescues and rehabilitates previously adopted mustangs, offering adoption or lifetime care.

shelters.name: Bagaduce River Equine Rescue
shelters.description: 501(c)(3) providing food, shelter, farrier and veterinary care to horses and donkeys in need. Finds safe, knowledgeable homes after rehabilitation.

shelters.name: Downeast Equine
shelters.description: Equine rescue organization serving the Downeast Maine region providing care and rehoming for horses in need.

shelters.name: First Light Farm Equine Shelter
shelters.description: Offers Emergency Feed Fund providing up to 10 bales of hay and 2 bags of grain (up to $75) to horse owners facing financial hardship.

shelters.name: Farm Animal Rescue of Maine
shelters.description: Non-profit animal rescue and sanctuary providing stable, loving environment for abused, neglected, or surrendered farm animals.

shelters.name: Community Spay-Neuter Clinic
shelters.description: Has spayed/neutered 35,000+ pets in Maine. Provides low-cost services for cat-only spay/neuter. Also operates mobile clinic in Waterville.

shelters.name: Rozzie May Animal Alliance
shelters.description: Leader in spay/neuter in New Hampshire and western Maine. Travels to various locations providing low-cost services for cats and dogs.

shelters.name: Darrowby Farm Sanctuary
shelters.description: Farm sanctuary providing compassionate care for all animals. Operates spay, neuter, and medical procedures for feral cats.

shelters.name: Save Our Strays
shelters.description: Cat rescue organization serving the Fairfield and central Maine area, focused on saving stray and homeless cats.

shelters.name: Acadia Wildlife Center
shelters.description: Started in 1994 to care for injured or orphaned native wildlife. Licensed by Maine Inland Fisheries and Wildlife and the federal government.

notes: Comprehensive collection of Maine animal shelters, humane societies, SPCAs, rescue organizations, wildlife rehabilitation centers, equine rescues, farm sanctuaries, and spay/neuter clinics. Includes both municipal shelters and nonprofit rescue organizations across the state from Portland to Aroostook County. Notable organizations include Peace Ridge Sanctuary (GFAS-accredited, 2024 Outstanding Sanctuary of the Year), Avian Haven (largest avian rehab in New England, 34,000+ birds treated), and Center for Wildlife (90,000+ animals over 39 years). Many foster-based rescues transport dogs from southern high-kill shelters.
